distinguishing_features: Active closed-loop actuation that dynamically re-stresses the gasket via a pneumatic bladder, rather than passive monitoring/inference as in all three prior arts
Uses chamber exhaust flow rate as the primary actuator signal to modulate seal contact pressure in real time
Adds new physical hardware (bladder actuator, solenoid valve, MCU) to change the seal's mechanical state, whereas prior arts are software-only diagnostic schemes on existing telemetry
Targets prevention of leak by compensating thermal/mechanical relaxation, not early warning or shutdown scheduling
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to actively maintain seal contact pressure during high-flow, high-vacuum operation so that outgassing/permeation-driven leak rate drift is compensated in real time rather than merely detected.
parsed.viable_reason: The stated physics is self-contradictory and likely inverted: high exhaust flow during pump-down does not imply high permeation risk (permeation-dominated regime occurs at low flow/high vacuum), and a pneumatic bladder adjusting gasket pre-load cannot meaningfully compensate permeation flux through the elastomer body, which is not controlled by contact pressure; thus the mechanism is physically implausible as the stated cure for the stated failure mode.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Active flow-rate-triggered pneumatic re-stressing of a vacuum gasket is not taught or suggested by the passive monitoring/inference approaches of the prior arts, so the distinguishing actuation mechanism itself is not an obvious step from the closest art.
